findings.obligation: L4 and doc of BuildCycleTimeOutliers: an unknown or invalid named Cycle Time has no limits
findings.observation: Only the unknown id is exercised (UnknownCycleTimeDefinition = 9999). The disjunct '!owner.IsCycleTimeDefinitionValid(definition)' (existing definition with invalid states) has no row and can be deleted with all tests green. Also the baseline length is pinned only at 10 and 14 days (13 vs 14 not pinned; existing ResolveBaseline rule, low), and the no-limits copy is asserted only in default words (NO_LIMITS_TEXT = /^No outliers: the Cycle Time process behaviour chart has no limits for this date range\.?$/), so a hard-coded 'Cycle Time' would pass. Severity medium/low.
findings.remediation: Add a row with an existing named Cycle Time whose end state is invalid expecting NoLimits; add a 13-day baseline row; add one renamed-term render asserting the no-limits sentence.

findings.location: TeamMetricsService.cs and PortfolioMetricsService.cs constructors 'ICycleTimeOutlierDefinition? outlierDefinition = null'; Program.cs 'builder.Services.AddSingleton(ICycleTimeOutlierDefinition.Default);'; CycleTimeScatterPlotChart.tsx 'wording.listTitle(analysis.cut ?? 0)'
findings.obligation: One owner of the default rule; wrong state hard to express (nw-code-craftsmanship SSOT, certainty by construction)
findings.observation: The default outlier definition is chosen in two places: Program registers ICycleTimeOutlierDefinition.Default and each service also falls back to it when the optional parameter is null ('outlierDefinition ?? ICycleTimeOutlierDefinition.Default'), so a missing or replaced registration is silently bypassed. The chart invents a 0-day limit for a null cut with 'analysis.cut ?? 0'. Severity low (RPP L1-L4).
findings.remediation: Make the definition a required constructor parameter in both services and drop the fallback; open the list title with a non-null limit by construction.
